correctness.rationale: The base-b carry identity d(n)=1-(b-1)nu_b(n+1) yields all possible two-letter increments. Shifting occurrences by t*b^K realizes every initial symbol residue, so F_2 and its reflection orbits are determined exactly by g=gcd(b-1,m). For b>=3, each length-four difference triple has two +1 entries while its reverse would force two -1; for b=2, an exhaustive even/odd start classification eliminates both reversal possibilities. This is an infinite local-pattern proof, not finite sampling. The length-three parity and carry analysis proves every reversible triple is a palindrome; a congruence j(b-1)=2 and alphabet translation give exactly 2m palindromes iff g divides 2. For m<=2, periodicity or palindromic iterates of the binary substitution establish reversal closure. The packaged verifier checks the exact orbit counts, explicit witnesses and finite cases.

originality.rationale: The primary 2024 paper introduces reflection complexity and poses its generalization to digit-sum words; it handles at most the binary-base example. Starosta supplies F_2 and generalized dihedral antimorphisms, and Allouche–Shallit classify infinite palindromicity, but neither proves the absence of nonpalindromic reversed pairs of length four or the 2-versus-4 arithmetic cutoff. Searches over direct and equivalent formulations found no covering statement. The previously covered binary-base special case and F_2 formula are acknowledged; full-text comparisons and residual risks are recorded.
residual_risks: A subsequently published or unindexed note might extract the same ordinary-reflection cutoff from the 2012 two-letter factor classification.
The cyclic/reversal-complexity bibliography was compared through indexed records rather than a full paper, although its invariant is not ordinary factor reversal.
The length-two factor set and binary-base special case are already covered and are not claimed as original; the genuinely new part is the all-base cutoff phase diagram.

value.rationale: The motivating 2024 paper explicitly asks how reflection complexity behaves under generalized Thue–Morse constructions. The complete two-parameter answer shows a natural qualitative arithmetic phase transition controlled by gcd(b-1,m): reversal closure, a sharp length-four avoidance threshold, or an earlier sharp length-two threshold. It yields the entire ordinary-reflection function for every m>=3 from a known factor complexity plus one exact small-length correction, not an arbitrary finite census or an incremental numerical gain.
